title: Enterprise procurement playbook + risk-tiering for vendor onboarding experiments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a pragmatic procurement and vendor onboarding playbook targeted at enterprise customers that (1) standardizes a SOC2-lite package and insurance requirements for small-to-mid vendors, (2) defines a risk-tiering matrix for faster procurement decisions, and (3) pilots an integrated vendor portal flow that automates questionnaire intake and contract template selection. This ticket covers discovery, two pricing/packaging experiments to reduce friction for lower-risk vendors, and handoff artifacts for Legal and Sales Ops.
acceptance_criteria: Draft playbook published to Confluence with step-by-step onboarding flows for low/medium/high risk vendors
Risk-tiering matrix (criteria + decision outcomes) reviewed and signed off by Security and Legal
Two pricing/packaging experiment designs documented with target cohorts and success metrics
Vendor portal prototype wireframes + intake form schema delivered to Eng and Design
One contract template (standard SaaS agreement + SOC2 addendum) prepared for pilot vendors
Automation checklist and ownership list assigned for pilot run
success_metrics: Reduce average procurement decision time for low-risk vendors from 18 days to <=7 days during pilot
Increase self-serve vendor completions via portal from 0% to >=45% for targeted cohort
Achieve 80% sign-off rate from Sales/Ops on contract template accuracy in pilot
No major security exceptions for pilot vendors (0 critical findings)
risks: Legal resource constraints delaying final contract language
Underestimated scope for portal automation could push Eng timeline
Insurance market variability could make standard thresholds unworkable for certain vendors
Security may require tighter SOC2 controls than the SOC2-lite package allows, increasing friction
comments: 2025-01-16 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff with Security and Legal completed. Security suggested a 3-tier risk model (Low/Medium/High) and asked for concrete control mappings to SOC2 controls. Legal requested a SOC2 addendum draft by 2025-01-28.

2025-01-22 - Miguel Torres: Scoped two pricing experiments: (A) flat onboarding fee waiver for verified low-risk vendors; (B) tiered support credits for mid-risk vendors in exchange for additional attestation. Documented cohorts and instrumentation plan in Confluence.

2025-01-29 - Claire Huang (Legal): Provided comments on contract template. Key ask: make insurance minimums explicit and add a fallback clause for vendors unable to obtain primary insurance. See linked doc for line-level edits.

2025-02-03 - Rajiv Menon (Sales Ops): Shared procurement SLA expectations for enterprise customers. Suggested pilot focus on non-core infra partners and marketplace integrations to minimize revenue risk.

2025-02-07 - Miguel Torres: Design handed off to Eng. Wireframes include a single intake form that branches by risk tier and surface required artifacts. Prototype ticket raised: ENG-3912. Added instrumentation hooks for time-to-complete and drop-off rates.

2025-02-10 - Security review: Initial SOC2-lite control mapping looks acceptable for Low tier. Security requested encrypted storage for vendor questionnaires and audit log retention policy; added to acceptance criteria.

2025-02-12 - Aisha Patel: Updated playbook draft with experiment measurement plan and pilot roll schedule. Next: Legal to finalize contract template (due 2025-02-21), Eng estimate confirmation (ENG-3912), and schedule pilot outreach with Partner Ops.
